messages:
maya: noticing a big backlog in the gpu provisioner queue for eu-west-1, nodes not coming up. pods Pending > 200 :thinking:
kevin: yep saw the Alertmanager spike. autoscaler is sending requests but cloud API is 429ing. logs show rate_limited from provider
aria: which pool/instance type? any pattern with spot vs on-demand?
sre-eli: mostly g4dn-type spot pools, but we have some on-demand p4 pools stuck too. suspect a provider-side leaky token bucket throttling our create calls
infra-jen: confirming — cloud support said there were transient create rate limits in the region earlier. we hit soft-limits for nodegroup create calls
maya: started cooling non-essential research jobs (label=research:sweep) using k8s eviction. applied a nodeSelector on new jobs to avoid pending churn
kevin: can we temporarily drain low-priority nodepools to free up slots for dedicated inference? or use taints+tolerations to move critical pods?
aria: plan: 1) cordon and drain research pools 2) spin up a small emergency on-demand nodepool with different instance family (c5->p3-type fallback) 3) reduce autoscaler burst flags
sre-eli: drafted commands:

```
kubectl label nodepool research enabled=false --overwrite
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

but we should avoid mass-drain scatter causing more creates
infra-jen: deploy-bot: created emergency nodepool `eu-pool-emergency-01` with 3 on-demand GPUs, instance-type p3.2xlarge
ops-bot: cloud-api: 2023-11-01T14:02:10Z createNodeGroup request accepted (id: ng-emer-01)
kevin: good. also lowering cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m? or that will cause churn
sre-eli: don't touch scale-down too aggressive. instead set --max-node-provision-time to 20m so we don't keep retrying too fast. also throttle autoscaler concurrency: --max-simultaneous-provisions=2
maya: applied a temporary mutation to the Karpenter/provisioner config to add backoff and jitter
aria: logs snippet from provisioner:

```
ProvisionerController: failed to CreateInstance: RateLimitExceeded: request throttled
backoff: next attempt in 45s
```

so it's clearly provider-side
kevin: can we switch some critical pods to use smaller batch sizes to reduce GPU memory footprint and fit on existing nodes? quick hotfix
maya: yes, pushed a runtime flag to the model service to halve batch_size for priority routes — reduced GPU memory by ~30%
sre-eli: another angle: enable fallback to cpu for low-QPS endpoints and mark them with a FeatureFlag so we can revert
infra-jen: cloud support responded: "we're currently enforcing a soft token bucket for node creation. we can raise the burst quota for your account but it'll take 2-3 hours" :exclamation:
aria: since waiting hours is bad, we need local mitigations only
kevin: propose a short-lived eviction policy: move all pods with annotation noncritical=true to nodepool-research and then cordon the research pool to stop new creations
maya: doing that now. running:

```
kubectl get pods -l noncritical=true -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl evict --force
```

aria: got some evict errors for pods with local volumes, skipping those
sre-eli: also seeing kube-scheduler backlog: Preemption TTL increasing. we should enable prioritized preemption for critical classes
infra-jen: made the new nodepool available for scheduling. nodes are Ready but Kubelet registration is slow on a couple
ops-bot: node ng-emer-01-0 Ready
ops-bot: node ng-emer-01-1 Ready
ops-bot: node ng-emer-01-2 Ready
maya: k8s started binding Pending pods to the emergency nodes. good - acceptance tests for inference passing
kevin: keep an eye on cloud-side rate limit counters. if we keep retrying creates we might extend the throttle window
aria: suggestion: batch provisioning attempts with exponential backoff and cap concurrency at 1 for the next 30m
sre-eli: changed autoscaler flags to --max-simultaneous-provisions=1 and --node-creation-backoff=60s
maya: monitoring token-level cost/latency dashboard — we're stable for critical routes but research backlog still huge
infra-jen: billing note — emergency on-demand nodes will bump this month's costs; we've tagged them emergency=true so finance can attribute
kevin: 👍 acceptable given SLA risk
aria: postmortem items:
- add per-region API create-rate alert
- pre-create warm nodepool reserves for burst risk workloads
- automation to switch lower-QPS routes to cpu fallback
- request quota raise from cloud (track request id)
sre-eli: also add a k8s admission webhook to tag noncritical job submissions so we can quickly bulk-evict next time
maya: added incident label and updated runbook: "if provider node create 429, create emergency nodepool with alternate instance family and throttle autoscaler" :memo:
infra-jen: opened cloud support ticket ID CS-48291 and requested quota bump; support ETA 3h
ops-bot: Alertmanager: severity=critical, rule=GPUPoolExhaustion, status=resolved -> firing count decreased
kevin: ok let's keep monitoring for 2 hours. if rate limits persist after cloud quota bump we escalate to provider engineer
aria: thanks everyone — great coordinated response. I'll draft the incident digest later
maya: leaving this thread open for final checks and the digest. :thumbsup:
alertmanager: system note: auto-closing silence in 4h if no further alerts
summary: incident thread: provisioner rate limiting caused gpu node creation stalls; emergency on-demand nodepool and eviction policies used as mitigation
